body_md:
# Track 2 Reference Scoring

This skill has two paired responsibilities:

1. Enrich Track 2 anchor references (or any CSV with DOIs) with two quality
   signals that a viva examiner will ask about: **citation count** and
   **venue quartile**. Signals live inside the same CSV so a later human
   reviewer can filter or sort without joining tables.
2. Produce a **per-reference inclusion-decision markdown** that pairs the
   numeric signals with a prose rationale explaining why the reference was
   purposively selected. The Track 2 CSV carries a path column pointing at
   this markdown, so the numeric row and the defensible rationale stay
   linked in the audit trail.

## When to use

- Immediately before or after a block of references is added to a Track 2
  identification log (typically the ESGCI DBA
  `01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv`).
- Retrospectively when new signals are wanted for rows added under an earlier
  drafting pass (Block A was added on 2026-09-02 before this skill existed).
- Any time SJR publishes a new annual CSV and quartile ranks need refreshing.

## Signals collected

| Column added to target CSV | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `s2_citation_count` | Semantic Scholar Graph API | Total citations tracked by S2. Comparable to Google Scholar for most CS and management refs; more comprehensive than the Crossref `is-referenced-by-count`. |
| `s2_influential_citations` | Semantic Scholar Graph API | S2's own quality-weighted count. Citations where the paper is materially engaged with, not just listed. |
| `s2_venue_name` | Semantic Scholar Graph API | Sanity-check field; disagreement with the CSV's `venue` column flags a metadata error. |
| `sjr_quartile` | SJR CSV lookup by ISSN | `Q1`, `Q2`, `Q3`, or `Q4`. `n_a` for books, reports, and preprints. `not_found` when the venue is not in the SJR set. |
| `sjr_year` | Constant taken from SJR CSV filename | Whichever annual snapshot is used. |
| `stats_retrieved_date` | Skill run date | Provenance. |
| `inclusion_decision_path` | Path to the per-reference decision markdown | Relative to `consensus-queries/` (e.g., `prisma-track2-inclusion-decisions/T2-B01_bacchelli_bird_2013.md`). Blank until a decision markdown is written. |
| `research_unit` | Manual classification by the triage reviewer | One of `developer`, `team`, `repository`, `organization`, `ai_system_output`, or `theory_anchor`. See the research-unit screen below. |
| `unit_alignment` | Manual classification by the triage reviewer | One of `aligned`, `partial`, `mismatch`, `neutral`, or `n_a`. Records whether the reference's research unit lines up with the thesis' repository-level design. |
| `psychology_adjacent` | Manual classification by the triage reviewer | One of `no`, `borderline`, or `yes`. Records whether the reference draws on psychology-adjacent constructs that the ESGCI DBA thesis has explicitly ruled out of scope. |
| `screening_notes` | Manual free-text by the triage reviewer | Prose caveat that names the framing constraint under which a mismatched or borderline reference is used (e.g., "cite for MCR construct only; do not extend to repository-level defect outcomes"). |

## API and data prerequisites

- Semantic Scholar API key in the workspace `.env` as `S2_API_KEY`. The
  `fetch_abstracts.py` skill already uses this key with the same rate-limit
  posture (1.2 s minimum interval, `Retry-After`-aware).
- The SJR annual CSV at
  `G:\My Drive\ESGCIDBA\correctness-wedge\thesis-review-method\consensus-queries\logs\scimagojr 2025.csv`
  (or override via `--sjr-csv`). The CSV uses `;` as delimiter and
  comma decimal separators. Key columns: `Issn`, `SJR Best Quartile`. ISSN
  values in this file have no hyphen and are comma-separated when a venue
  has both print and electronic ISSNs.

## Input CSV expectations

The target CSV must have at least:

- `anchor_id` — unique row identifier
- `doi_url` — full DOI URL for lookup (empty allowed for books and reports)

Any additional columns are preserved. On update the new signal columns are
appended if absent, or overwritten for the targeted rows.

## CLI

```powershell
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" `
    ".github\skills\track2-reference-scoring\scripts\enrich_track2_anchors.py" `
    --csv "G:\...\logs\prisma-logs\01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv"
```

Optional flags:

- `--anchor-ids T2-A01,T2-A02,...` — score only the listed rows. Default is
  every row that does not yet have `s2_citation_count` populated.
- `--force` — re-fetch even for rows already scored (useful when SJR changes
  year or when metadata needs correction).
- `--sjr-csv <path>` — override the default SJR file path.
- `--sjr-year <YYYY>` — override the year written into the `sjr_year` column;
  default is inferred from the SJR filename.

## Behaviour

For each targeted row:

1. Read the DOI from `doi_url`. If empty (book, report, preprint without a
   DOI), skip S2 and SJR lookups. Write `n_a` for `sjr_quartile` and leave
   citation columns as empty strings.
2. Call Semantic Scholar Graph API for the DOI at
   `https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:{doi}?fields=citationCount,influentialCitationCount,venue,publicationVenue`.
   Respect the 2.0 s interval and the `Retry-After` header. Retry up to three
   times on 429.
3. Extract `citationCount`, `influentialCitationCount`, `venue.name` (or
   `publicationVenue.name`), and any ISSN present in
   `publicationVenue.issn`, `publicationVenue.issnPrint`,
   `publicationVenue.issnElectronic`, or the `publicationVenue.alternate_issns`
   list. S2 sometimes files the SJR-matching ISSN under `alternate_issns` for
   long-running journals (Science being one example).
4. If S2 returns no ISSN, fall back to Crossref (`/works/{doi}`) for the
   ISSN list. Crossref reliably returns both print and electronic ISSNs when
   the paper is indexed.
5. Normalise each ISSN candidate (strip hyphens, upper-case) and look it up
   in the SJR `Issn` column. Return the `SJR Best Quartile` value at the
   first hit.
6. If neither S2 nor Crossref yields an ISSN match, fall back to a
   case-insensitive title match against SJR's `Title` column, using first
   the S2-returned venue name and then the CSV row's own `venue` field.
   This rescues cases where the DOI itself is missing from S2 and Crossref
   (pre-2005 MIT Press QJE DOIs are the recurring example).
7. Write updated rows atomically (tmp file, then replace) so an interrupted
   run leaves the CSV in a valid state.

## Failure modes and handling

- **S2 returns 404** for the DOI. Recorded as `s2_citation_count = 0`,
  `s2_influential_citations = 0`, and a note in stdout. Common for
  brand-new preprints and non-Crossref-indexed items.
- **S2 rate-limit exhausted** after two retries. Row is skipped, error logged
  to stdout. Re-run picks it up because the row still has empty stats.
- **SJR ISSN lookup fails**. `sjr_quartile = not_found`. Human triage step:
  check whether the venue is a conference series that SJR indexes under a
  different ISSN family (e.g., IEEE conference proceedings vs. IEEE
  Transactions journals).
- **Book or report reference**. Handled up-front: `sjr_quartile = n_a` and
  S2 fields left empty because DOI is empty.

## Related artefacts

- Target CSV lives at
  `consensus-queries/logs/prisma-logs/01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv`
  for Ch2 PRISMA, or `consensus-queries/logs/non-prisma-logs/ch3_methods_anchors.csv`
  for Ch3 anchors. The script accepts either.
- SJR CSV lives at `consensus-queries/logs/scimagojr 2025.csv`. Refresh with
  the next annual release from scimagojr.com when available.
- Inclusion-decision markdowns live at
  `consensus-queries/prisma-track2-inclusion-decisions/` (one file per anchor).

## Inclusion-decision markdown workflow

Every Track 2 row is paired with a per-reference decision markdown. The
workflow is:

1. **Fetch signals** for the candidate DOI (S2 citations, influential
   citations, venue, SJR quartile) using the classes in
   `scripts/enrich_track2_anchors.py`. This can happen ahead of the
   discussion via a probe script when a whole block is being triaged.
2. **Draft the decision markdown** in chat, using the template below.
   The draft is shown to the user for approval before anything is written.
3. **On approval, write the markdown to disk** at
   `consensus-queries/prisma-track2-inclusion-decisions/<anchor_id>_<first_author>_<coauthor_or_etal>_<year>.md`,
   e.g., `T2-B01_bacchelli_bird_2013.md` or `T2-A05_brynjolfsson_etal_2023.md`.
4. **Update the Track 2 CSV row**: append the new row (or edit an existing
   one) and populate `inclusion_decision_path` with the relative path from
   `consensus-queries/`.
5. **Rejected candidates** get a decision markdown too, filed under
   `consensus-queries/prisma-track2-inclusion-decisions/rejected/`. They
   never enter the Track 2 CSV, but the rationale is preserved so the same
   candidate is not relitigated later.

### Inclusion-decision markdown template

```markdown
# <anchor_id> — <First author> & <coauthor or et al.> (<year>), "<title>"

**Status:** Marked for Track 2 inclusion (<YYYY-MM-DD>). Not yet written to `01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv`.

## Bibliographic entry

<APA 7 reference>

**DOI:** `<bare DOI>`

## Quality signals (retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>)

| Signal | Value |
|---|---|
| Semantic Scholar total citations | <n> |
| Semantic Scholar influential citations | <n> |
| Venue | <venue name and short qualifier> |
| Venue tier | <CORE rank for conferences, or "n/a"> |
| SJR quartile | <Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 or n/a with one-line reason> |

## Why it matters for the correctness wedge

<2-4 sentences. State the paper's contribution in plain terms, then link it
to the thesis' correctness-versus-throughput argument. Name the mechanism
the paper supplies (measurement construct, empirical finding, theory
anchor, method precedent).>

## Fit vs Ch2 sections

- <Which Ch2 section or paragraph the paper anchors.>
- <What claim it lets the thesis make that would otherwise be unsupported.>
- <Whether omitting it would create a viva-defensibility gap.>

## Track 2 categorisation (proposed)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `anchor_id` | `<T2-BXX>` |
| `category` | `<slug matching existing Block A categories or a new one>` |
| `register` | `recommended_addition` \| `valid_carryover` |
| `source_method` | `purposive_selection` \| `backward_snowballing` |
| `discovery_provenance` | <One-line note on where the reference surfaced.> |
| `target_chapter` | Ch2 (<section slug>) \| Ch3 (<section slug>) |

## Research unit and screening

| Screen | Value |
|---|---|
| `research_unit` | `developer` \| `team` \| `repository` \| `organization` \| `ai_system_output` \| `theory_anchor` |
| `unit_alignment` | `aligned` \| `partial` \| `mismatch` \| `neutral` \| `n_a` |
| `psychology_adjacent` | `no` \| `borderline` \| `yes` |

**Note.** <One or two sentences naming the framing constraint under which a `mismatch`, `partial`, or `borderline` reference is used. Omit if the classification is `aligned` and `no`.>

## Decision rationale

<2-4 sentences integrating the numeric signals with the fit argument.
State the decision (include or reject) and the counterfactual: what would
happen at viva if this reference were omitted, or what alternative anchor
covers the same ground.>

**Decision:** <Include in Track 2 | Reject; file in rejected/>
```

House-style rules (from `CLAUDE.md` §5) apply to every decision markdown:
British English, no em dashes, no invented compound-modifier hyphens, no
AI-tooling tells, no forbidden vocabulary. The orchestrator style-verification
pass runs before writing to disk.

### Retrospective coverage

Rows added before the decision markdown workflow existed (Block A on
2026-09-02) get a retrospective pass: for each row, draft a decision
markdown using the same template, show the user, and on approval write the
markdown to disk and populate `inclusion_decision_path`. The retrospective
pass runs after the current triage block is finished so state is not mixed
between prospective and retrospective decisions.

## Screening protocol

Every non-theory Track 2 candidate must pass two additional screens before
being written to the CSV. Both screens are recorded in dedicated columns
(`research_unit`, `unit_alignment`, `psychology_adjacent`, `screening_notes`)
and reproduced in the "Research unit and screening" section of the
inclusion-decision markdown.

### Screen 1: research-unit alignment

Classify the reference's primary research unit into one of:

- `developer` — individual-developer sampling, interviews, surveys, or
  experiments where the person is the unit of analysis.
- `team` — team-level case studies or trade-off models where the team is
  the unit of analysis.
- `repository` — project-level or file-level modelling where the
  codebase is the unit of analysis.
- `organization` — firm-level, multi-firm, or industrial-practice
  studies where the organization is the unit of analysis.
- `ai_system_output` — audits or evaluations of an AI system's output
  (e.g., Copilot's code, a DL reviewer's suggestions) where the object of
  study is the model output rather than a human unit.
- `theory_anchor` — theoretical framing paper; the screen does not apply.

Then map the classification to `unit_alignment` against the thesis' design
(repository-level with corporate-sponsored OSS as the identifying context):

- `aligned` — `repository` or `organization`. Organization is a proxy for
  the corporate-sponsorship dimension of the repository-level design.
- `partial` — `team`. Team is a proxy for repository but not identical.
- `mismatch` — `developer`. The reference is at the wrong unit of
  analysis for the repository-level design. This does not disqualify the
  reference, but it forces a framing constraint: the reference is cited
  for the construct or as motivation, not as evidence for repository-level
  claims.
- `neutral` — `ai_system_output`. No human unit, so the alignment screen
  does not apply.
- `n_a` — `theory_anchor`.

The `screening_notes` column names the framing constraint under which a
`mismatch` or `partial` reference is used.

### Screen 2: psychology-adjacent filter

Classify each reference for psychology-adjacent construct dependence:

- `no` — the reference does not rely on individual psychological
  constructs (motivation, burnout, self-determination, developer
  experience as a psychological state, engagement, etc.).
- `borderline` — the reference uses self-report or perception
  methodology but the analytical claim is an organisational or empirical
  one (e.g., self-reported productivity correlated with codebase
  quality). Requires a framing sentence in the decision markdown that
  names why the psychology-adjacent methodology does not import a
  psychology-adjacent claim into the thesis.
- `yes` — the reference's core construct is psychology-adjacent (JD-R,
  self-determination theory, developer wellbeing, motivation
  frameworks). These references are rejected from Track 2 under the
  ESGCI DBA thesis' explicit scope exclusion of psychology-adjacent
  constructs.

Any reference classified `psychology_adjacent = yes` is routed to the
`prisma-track2-inclusion-decisions/rejected/` folder with a rejection
markdown documenting the scope-exclusion rationale.

### When the screens run

The two screens run at the same triage step as the venue-and-signal
review. The `research_unit` and `psychology_adjacent` classifications are
part of the triage prompt to the user, alongside the signal profile. The
decision markdown template's "Research unit and screening" section is
populated on approval.

Rows added before the screens existed (Blocks A through D on 2026-09-02
were added before the screens were adopted) get a retrospective
classification pass in the same style as the inclusion-decision markdown
retrospective pass.

## History

- 2026-09-02 — Skill created. Initial columns and CLI as documented above.
  Block A of the Track 2 identification log (T2-A01 through T2-A09) was
  scored retrospectively on the same day.
- 2026-09-02 — Extended with the inclusion-decision markdown workflow.
  Added `inclusion_decision_path` column to the target CSV schema. Block B
  triage (T2-B01 onward) is the first block to use the paired
  markdown-plus-CSV workflow. Block A rows will be revisited retrospectively
  after Block B is complete so each existing row also carries a decision
  markdown link.
- 2026-09-02 — Added the research-unit alignment screen and the
  psychology-adjacent filter, with four new CSV columns
  (`research_unit`, `unit_alignment`, `psychology_adjacent`,
  `screening_notes`) and a matching "Research unit and screening"
  section in the inclusion-decision markdown. All 22 rows already in the
  CSV received a retrospective classification pass on the same day.
- 2026-09-02 — File-naming schema swapped so Track 2 anchors are now
  `01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv` (from `01c_...`) and the Track 1
  dedup output is `01c_identification_dedup.csv` (from `01b_...`). The
  new alphabetical order reflects PRISMA processing order: Track 2 anchors
  are established first, then the `consensus-search-log` extractor runs
  Track 1 dedup against them, tagging any DOI overlap in a new
  `track2_status` column on the Track 1 dedup CSV. Overlapping records are
  excluded from title+abstract screening because they are already under
  full-paper review under the Track 2 purposive-selection arm.
- 2026-09-02 — subject to `csv-log-discipline.instructions.md`. The
  `01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv` now carries a `stable_id` column
  (8-hex MD5 of the anchor's identity key) alongside its `anchor_id`.
  `anchor_id` is immutable once assigned: retired anchors get a tombstone
  (`status=retired`), never a slot recycle. The Track 2 decision markdowns
  under `prisma-track2-inclusion-decisions/` remain the source of truth for
  the prose rationale; the corpus contract (H1 anchor_id, `**DOI:**` line,
  filename prefix) is enforced by `.github/skills/consensus-search-log/scripts/csv_lint.py`.
  Any script that mutates `01b` must acquire the `.pid` lockfile next to
  the CSV.
